title: RWB-S8-E2036-APP: the deviation hold that the queue-write interface obeys has no published element names, no case-event names, no case-side setter for deviation_open and no placement-half criteria, and the pattern set adds dependencies the metadata rows do not carry
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.7, R7.1, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S8-E2036-APP; context pack S8 rwb-deviation (service row, ownership rows, naming rules, Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 5, 8 and 13, Temporal and Drools slides 5, 8 and 13, connection-matrix row S8); legacy RWB-E2-036 Queue write interface for models and agents v1, sections 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 15; FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A1.4, A2.1 to A2.9 and Screens; TSD S8 Deviation handling v2 T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-03, R-DEV-08, R-DEV-09 and R-DEV-18; LDM and Data Dictionary v8 deviation DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 and recovery_case DF-CAS-019; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-06 and EV-07; RWB-P3-E2036-APP and RWB-P2-E2036-CON as written in this run
section: Metadata (Dependencies, Patterns applied); Sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12.1 to 12.9, 13, 15, 18 and 19
description: (1) The hold is carried on the two events the Ownership Map gives S8, DeviationRaised (EV-06) and DeviationCleared (EV-07), with an open-deviation count, the handler and the return point, but no source publishes an AsyncAPI document or an element set for either envelope: the ids and the names are published and their properties are not. The same is true of the facts' JSON names and of the refusal element of the rwb-integration placement contract, which is the one message the hold reason has to agree with. (2) The consumer is rwb-case, which holds recovery_case.deviation_open (DF-CAS-019) and refuses a placement on it without a synchronous call (RWB-P3-E2036-APP), yet no source publishes a case event that names the set or the clear of that flag, and no source publishes a case operation that sets it: the hand-over is an event contract that neither side publishes in full. (3) The split plan allocates no legacy acceptance criterion to this slice and still lists all fourteen legacy test ids, so the fourteen cases belong to the key and only the deviation cases are this slice's; the placement cases are proved by rwb-case and the end-to-end copies by RWB-ITG-E2036-ITG, and no source states which slice owns which case. (4) R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 move the remaining codes from DEV_FLAGGED to DEV_WITH_OWNER in TSD S8 T4, but their conditions are set only in the Business Rules and Routing Logic workbook, which is not among the files read for this story; the six rows this story evaluates are the six whose conditions the FSD and TSD publish, and the routing of X4 to X7 is not restated. (5) The pattern set of the plan adds ten decoupling patterns and the plan's H row is empty: DP-03, DP-07, DP-08, DP-09, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 each add an H row to a platform or service contract story and DP-07 and DP-08 each add a C row, so the metadata table and section 13 disagree by construction unless the H and C rows are read as held by the platform. (6) The legacy story places the interface in the P2 backlog while the WP builds it in rwb-deviation, and the two operations the service keeps are RWB-S8-E7001-APP's; this slice therefore declares no operation of its own, which no source states either.
evidence: Context pack S8 ownership rows: one table (deviation), two REST operations (PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}, POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations), two events (EV-06, EV-07), no job, one workflow; connection-matrix row S8: E to P3, R and E to P1, T and E to P10, nothing to a placement read; Architecture v5 slide 13 notes (the deviation is a signal; the workflow pauses the stage timer and not the prescription timer); TSD S8 T3.1 (ten deviation fields, no counter column), T3.2 (the three lists), T4 (22 DEV rules over 9 states, R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 without published conditions), T5.3 (the two event names), T6.1 (RW-CONDUCT R only); FSD S8 A2.9 (two deviations on one case, resume only when all are cleared) and A2.2.4.2 (on-hold banner, MSG-P3-004); legacy RWB-E2-036 section 8 BR4, section 10, section 15 and section 16; RWB-P3-E2036-APP step 6 of its flow and its X6 (refusal on the case flag, no call to rwb-deviation); split plan slice RWB-S8-E2036-APP (H [], C [RWB-P2-E2036-CON], acs [], fourteen tcs, ten patterns)
area: Event contract detail, case boundary and slice allocation
proposed: Publish the hold element in the event catalogue and in the service contract: case reference, deviation reference, code, open count, handler, return point, contact-stop flag and rule version, additive inside major version 1 of rwb.deviation.events.v1, with the case-event subscription of the case router declared against the same catalogue. Have the rwb-case owner declare the event-driven set and clear of recovery_case.deviation_open, so the flag is a published behaviour and not an assumption. Keep the metadata rows exactly as the plan gives them and read the seven H rows and the two C rows of section 13 as dependencies the platform and service contract stories hold, with the one legacy contract edge RWB-P2-E2036-CON in the metadata. Record in the Service Story Catalog which slice proves which legacy test case: the deviation cases here, the placement cases in rwb-case, the end-to-end copies in RWB-ITG-E2036-ITG. Reconfirm the X4 to X7 routing rows against the Business Rules and Routing Logic workbook before wave 2 closes; this story restates none of them.
